filename: 2025-Huang-Values in the Wild Discovering and Analyzing Values in Real AI.md

dataset_size: 3,307 unique AI values extracted from hundreds of thousands of conversations
reasoning: Develops a novel empirical framework for mapping and measuring AI values in deployment, creating a taxonomy of 3,307 values and analyzing how they vary by context. This is a value evaluation methodology applied to real-world LLM interactions.

what_measures: Moral reasoning patterns in LLMs - utilitarian vs deontological responses to personal and impersonal moral dilemmas

reasoning: Conducts systematic empirical evaluation of seven LLMs using structured moral dilemmas under different ethical framings (deontological and utilitarian), comparing LLM moral reasoning to human patterns.

filename: 2025-Hähnel-A Companion to Applied Philosophy of AI.md

This constitutes an evaluation framework for assessing LLMs on ethical standards in mental health.

Industry-level safety assessment of AI companies' practices using 34 governance indicators. Evaluates corporate safety practices and policies, not LLM moral reasoning or ethical decision-making capabilities directly.

FACTS Grounding benchmarks LLMs on factual accuracy/grounding in long-form text generation. It measures hallucination/faithfulness to source documents, not moral reasoning, ethical judgment, or value alignment.

reasoning: Introduces a novel framework for continuously evaluating moral stability and ethical coherence in LLMs. While dataset-free, it creates an evaluation pipeline that generates and assesses ethical scenarios to measure moral consistency.

what_measures: Moral consistency and ethical stability of LLMs across contexts and temporal scales
how_measures: Three-layer closed-loop framework: lexical integrity analysis, semantic risk estimation, reasoning-based judgment modeling; autonomously generates ethical scenarios
reasoning: Duplicate of MoCoP paper above (same arXiv URL). Proposes a framework for continuous ethical evaluation of LLMs measuring moral coherence.

what_measures: Safety alignment in LLMs - helpfulness vs harmlessness tradeoff across 19 harm categories with three severity levels

SPARTA ALIGNMENT is a multi-model self-alignment algorithm where LLMs compete to improve general instruction-following. While it uses NormAd as one of 12 evaluation tasks, it does not create a new ethics benchmark or evaluation - it is an alignment training method, not an evaluation instrument.

what_measures: Moral reasoning capabilities of LLMs across three dimensions: foundational moral principles, reasoning robustness, and value consistency
how_measures: Three-dimensional framework using modified measures from moral psychology (MFQ, Moral Dilemmas, WVS); quantifies alignment with human ethical standards
reasoning: Creates a novel three-dimensional framework for evaluating moral reasoning in LLMs using established moral psychology instruments (MFQ, WVS). Publicly released benchmark and codebase.

what_measures: Moral reasoning capabilities across foundational moral principles, reasoning robustness, and value consistency

MASLegalBench is a legal reasoning benchmark for multi-agent LLM systems focused on GDPR compliance. While it involves legal/regulatory reasoning, it tests legal knowledge and deductive reasoning rather than moral reasoning, ethical judgment, or value alignment.

CogniModal-D is a multimodal dataset for human deception detection using physiological/behavioral signals (EEG, ECG, etc.) from human subjects. It does not evaluate AI/LLM moral reasoning or ethical decision-making - it uses ML for lie detection in humans.

what_measures: Moral preferences of LLMs grounded in Moral Foundations Theory (six core foundations) - revealed moral preferences and consistency across dilemma variations

models_evaluated: State-of-the-art LLMs (not specified by name in abstract)
reasoning: Introduces MFD-LLM dataset grounded in Moral Foundations Theory to evaluate LLM moral preferences and consistency. Proposes a novel evaluation method that captures the full spectrum of moral preferences.
